entries.title: I Corinthians 9:1
segments: Have I not seen Jesus our Lord, etc.  Paul here discusses his apostolic authority and conduct, evidently in answer to objections brought by some of the opposing parties mentioned in

, and perhaps mentioned in the Corinthians' letter of inquiry, 'the things whereof ye wrote.' Those who called themselves 'of Cephas' and 'of Christ' apparently objected to Paul that he was not one of the original twelve, and had not attended the personal ministry of Jesus.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:2
segments: The seal of mine apostleship. The fact that God had so blessed his labors as to lead the Corinthians to Christ proved Paul's call to be genuine.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:3
segments:
Defence. Probably referring to what follows.
 

 
 Them that examine me. Those who sit in Judgment on me; the opposers already mentioned.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:4
segments: To eat and to drink. That is, to receive food and drink at the cost of the church; a right given by Christ himself (

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:5
segments: To lead about a wife. Not only to be married, but to be accompanied by one's wife in ministerial travels among the churches, both being supported by the church, as indicated by

.
 

 
 The rest of the apostles, etc.  Plainly showing that these were married, notably Cephas or Peter (Mk 1.30, 31).

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:6
segments: Working. That is, for our own support, while preaching the gospel (

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:7
segments:
:14
 
 What soldier ever serveth, etc.  These verses contain a defence of the right of ministerial support.  Paul feared lest his example should be pleaded against that right.
 

 
 Carnal things. Earthly enjoyments and supplies.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:16
segments: Woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel.  Not a statement of the universal ministerial call, but of the condemnation which had stricken him down as a persecutor, and of the obligation which laid upon him at his conversion the necessity of preaching the gospel.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:18
segments: My reward.  No earthly recompense, but the privilege of giving the gospel freely to men.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:20
segments: Became as a Jew.  In all innocent compliances.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:21
segments:
Them that are without law.  Those who are without the ceremonial law; the Gentiles.
 

 
 Not being without law to God.  Never disobeying the moral law, but pushing the ceremonial law aside in order to win those who have never been bound by it.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:22
segments: Gain the weak. With all generous and self denying consideration of the needs of their weakness (

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:23
segments: That I may be a joint partaker thereof.  Win the gospel's glorious reward.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:25
segments:
Exerciseth self-control in all things. The comparison is to the Isthmian games celebrated with great splendor at Corinth.  The athletes of that day, as of our own, denied themselves every indulgence that would hinder them from winning the prize.
 

 
 A corruptible crown.  A fading wreath.  The prize in the games was a wreath of laurel, wild olive, pine, or sometimes only of parsley.
 

 
 But we an incorruptible. (

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:26
segments: As not beating the air.  The figure changes to that of the boxer.  Not like such a one 'beating the air' with empty flourishes while no antagonist is within reach.

entries.title: I Corinthians 9:27
segments:
I buffet my body.  I beat down all bodily appetites and desires.
 

 
 Bring it onto bondage.  Reduce the physical into entire subjection to the spiritual nature.
 

 
 After that I have preached to others. See
Rejected. Either as unworthy to be a preacher or unworthy of the crown of life.
